\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{خیانت} \fa{کردن} (khiyânat kardan)}{خیانت کردن (khiyânat kardan)}]{\fa{خیانت} \fa{کردن} (khiyânat kardan) — to betray}

\label{lesson:FA-C349-khiyanat-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a treasure, then the Persian for fate.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{خیانت} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{خیانت} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{khiyânat kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to betray\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{برادرش} \fa{به} \fa{او} \fa{خیانت} \fa{کرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Barâdarash be u khiyânat kard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
His brother betrayed him.
\end{quote}

The person betrayed takes \emph{be}. Present \emph{khiyânat mikonad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{khiyânat} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{khiyāna}, \textquotedblleft{}treason, betrayal\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{kardan} \textquotedblleft{}to do\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khiyânat kardan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khiyânat kardan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{khiyânat kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a treasure, then the Persian for fate, then say \emph{khiyânat kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{انتقام} \fa{گرفتن} (enteqâm gereftan)}{انتقام گرفتن (enteqâm gereftan)}]{\fa{انتقام} \fa{گرفتن} (enteqâm gereftan) — to take revenge, to avenge}

\label{lesson:FA-C349-enteqam-gereftan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fate, then the Persian for to betray.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{انتقام} \fa{گرفتن}}
\textbf{\fa{انتقام} \fa{گرفتن}} (\emph{enteqâm gereftan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to take revenge, to avenge\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{سال} \fa{ها} \fa{بعد} \fa{انتقام} \fa{پدرش} \fa{را} \fa{گرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{U sâl-hâ ba'd enteqâm-e pedarash râ gereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Years later he avenged his father.
\end{quote}

\emph{Enteqâm-e kasi râ gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to avenge someone\textquotedblright{}; \emph{az kasi enteqâm gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take revenge on someone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{enteqâm} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{intiqām}, \textquotedblleft{}revenge\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB). \emph{gereftan} \textquotedblleft{}to take\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian, from the Old Persian root \emph{grab-}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{enteqâm gereftan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{enteqâm gereftan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for fate, then the Persian for to betray, then say \emph{enteqâm gereftan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{جنگیدن} (jangidan)}{جنگیدن (jangidan)}]{\fa{جنگیدن} (jangidan) — to fight}

\label{lesson:FA-C349-jangidan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to betray, then the Persian for to take revenge.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{جنگیدن}}
\textbf{\fa{جنگیدن}} (\emph{jangidan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to fight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سربازها} \fa{تا} \fa{صبح} \fa{جنگیدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sarbâz-hâ tâ sobh jangidand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The soldiers fought until morning.
\end{quote}

\emph{jang} \textquotedblleft{}war\textquotedblright{} + the verb suffix \emph{-idan}. Present \emph{mijangad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{jangidan} is built from Persian \emph{jang} \textquotedblleft{}war\textquotedblright{}, a native noun, turned into a verb with the suffix \emph{-idan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کشتن} (koshtan)}{کشتن (koshtan)}]{\fa{کشتن} (koshtan) — to kill}

\label{lesson:FA-C349-koshtan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to take revenge, then the Persian for to fight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کشتن}}
\textbf{\fa{کشتن}} (\emph{koshtan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to kill\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{پهلوان} \fa{اژدها} \fa{را} \fa{کشت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Pahlavân ezhdehâ râ kosht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The champion killed the dragon.
\end{quote}

Present stem \emph{kosh-}: \emph{mikoshad}. \emph{Koshte shodan} is \textquotedblleft{}to be killed\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{koshtan} is a native Persian verb with the present stem \emph{kosh-}; EtymDB lists it without a parent.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اسیر} \fa{شدن} (asir shodan)}{اسیر شدن (asir shodan)}]{\fa{اسیر} \fa{شدن} (asir shodan) — to be taken prisoner}

\label{lesson:FA-C349-asir-shodan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to fight, then the Persian for to kill.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اسیر} \fa{شدن}}
\textbf{\fa{اسیر} \fa{شدن}} (\emph{asir shodan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to be taken prisoner\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{سربازهای} \fa{زیادی} \fa{در} \fa{جنگ} \fa{اسیر} \fa{شدند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sarbâz-hâ-ye ziyâdi dar jang asir shodand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Many soldiers were taken prisoner in the war.
\end{quote}

\emph{Asir} \textquotedblleft{}a captive\textquotedblright{}. Present \emph{asir mishavad}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{asir} is borrowed from Arabic \emph{asīr}, \textquotedblleft{}captive, prisoner\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists the Arabic word). \emph{shodan} \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{} is inherited Persian.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
